settings.heading: The best years are the everyday ones.
settings.body: When you think about the future together, it isn't always about grand bucket-list trips. More often, it's about the quiet mornings over coffee, the afternoon walks, tending to the garden, and having the energy to choose how you spend your day. Preserving those ordinary, beautiful moments is why healthy aging matters. And healthy aging starts at the microscopic level—with how your body maintains its own cells.

settings.heading: The biology of aging: What is Autophagy?
settings.body: Your cells are constantly working, and over time, they accumulate wear and tear. To stay healthy, your body uses a built-in recycling program called autophagy. Think of it as a cellular cleanup crew. Autophagy breaks down damaged cellular parts and recycles them to maintain efficient function. As we get older, this natural maintenance process can slow down. That's why scientists studying longevity are so focused on finding ways to support autophagy.

settings.heading: Where spermidine fits into the picture.
settings.body: Spermidine is a naturally occurring polyamine found widely in nature and human biology. It plays an intimately researched role in how cells function and survive. In laboratory models, researchers have observed that spermidine actually induces autophagy. When the cellular recycling process was deliberately blocked in these models, the longevity benefits associated with spermidine disappeared. This tells scientists that spermidine is directly tied to the body's cellular maintenance pathways.

settings.heading: The human dietary connection.
settings.body: The interest in spermidine goes beyond the laboratory. A major 20-year observational study followed over 800 adults aged 45 to 84 to look at their diets. After adjusting for various lifestyle factors, researchers found that people who consumed higher amounts of spermidine through their regular food had a statistical association with lower mortality over the study period. While a dietary association doesn't prove that taking a supplement will add years to your life, it provides a compelling human reason to pay attention to this compound.
settings.sources: Prospective dietary cohort, 829 people aged 45–84, followed for up to 20 years; independent cohort validation ↗

settings.heading: The link to fasting and cellular health.
settings.body: You may have heard that intermittent fasting is popular in longevity circles. One of the reasons researchers study fasting is because going without food triggers the body's autophagy process. Interestingly, a 2024 study found that fasting actually raised spermidine levels in human volunteers. Furthermore, when researchers blocked the synthesis of spermidine in experimental models, the fasting-induced autophagy was impaired. Goodwell doesn't replace a healthy diet or the physiological effects of fasting, but it provides a compound intimately involved in those same biological pathways.
settings.sources: Fasting studies across organisms, human volunteers and human cells ↗

settings.heading: Early human research on cellular support.
settings.body: Beyond dietary associations, researchers are beginning to study oral spermidine supplements in humans. A pilot study randomized 40 adults over 65 across spermidine and placebo groups, with 38 analyzed. The active group took a wheat-germ extract supplying 6mg per day for 13 weeks. While the trial was small and exploratory, researchers observed autophagy-related biomarker changes in certain immune cells, with some specific responses concentrated in a subgroup of participants. This early research provides a concrete bridge between oral intake and cellular biology. Goodwell offers 10mg of Spermidine 3HCL to help you actively support your cellular maintenance as part of a broader lifestyle of good nutrition and exercise.
settings.sources: Randomized placebo-controlled pilot, 40 adults over 65, 6 mg/day in wheat-germ extract for 13 weeks ↗

settings.question: Will taking this make us live longer?
settings.answer: No supplement can guarantee a longer life. The research on spermidine shows it is involved in cellular maintenance (autophagy) and dietary studies associate higher intake with lower mortality. Goodwell is designed to support cellular health, not to serve as a magic pill for lifespan extension.
settings.sources: Prospective dietary cohort, 829 people aged 45–84, followed for up to 20 years; independent cohort validation ↗

settings.question: What exactly does 10mg Spermidine 3HCL mean?
settings.answer: Spermidine 3HCL (trihydrochloride) is the specific form of the ingredient used in our formulation. Each two-capsule serving provides 10mg of Spermidine 3HCL.

settings.question: How long does one bottle last?
settings.answer: One bottle contains 60 capsules. At the recommended serving size of 2 capsules per day, one bottle lasts one person for 30 days. For a couple taking it daily, you will need two bottles per month.

settings.question: Is this the same formulation used in the clinical trials?
settings.answer: Various studies use different forms and doses of spermidine, including food extracts, synthetic salts, and high-dose animal diets. Goodwell uses Spermidine 3HCL. While the ingredient itself is heavily researched, this specific formula has not been the subject of a dedicated lifespan clinical trial.
settings.sources: Randomized placebo-controlled pilot, 40 adults over 65, 6 mg/day in wheat-germ extract for 13 weeks ↗

settings.question: What is autophagy?
settings.answer: Autophagy is the body's natural process of breaking down and recycling old, damaged cellular components. It's a critical part of how your cells maintain themselves over time.

settings.question: Can we just get spermidine from food?
settings.answer: Yes, spermidine is found in foods like wheat germ, aged cheese, soybeans, and mushrooms. Many people choose a supplement to ensure they are getting a consistent, measurable amount every single day without altering their diet.
settings.sources: Prospective dietary cohort, 829 people aged 45–84, followed for up to 20 years; independent cohort validation ↗

settings.question: How quickly will we feel a difference?
settings.answer: Spermidine is studied for long-term cellular maintenance, not as a quick-fix stimulant. You are unlikely to 'feel' a sudden burst of energy. It is designed to be a consistent part of a long-term healthy aging routine.

settings.question: Are there any allergens in Goodwell?
settings.answer: The capsules contain Spermidine 3HCL, an HPMC (vegetarian) capsule, and rice flour. However, you should always check the label carefully and consult your doctor if you have severe allergies.

settings.question: Should we take this with food?
settings.answer: You can take Goodwell capsules with or without food, depending on your personal preference and how it settles in your stomach.

settings.question: Can this replace our current medications?
settings.answer: Absolutely not. Goodwell is a dietary supplement, not a medication. It is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease. Always discuss new supplements with your healthcare provider, especially if you take prescription medications.
